ambiguities.text: The order_index parameter for Unscheduled forks is not clearly documented for its intended use case
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume order_index is used to maintain relative ordering of multiple unscheduled forks when they are eventually scheduled. Higher indices come later.

ambiguities.text: The interaction between ByBlockNumber and ByTimestamp when both could technically apply to a block is not explicit
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume post-merge blocks only use ByTimestamp and pre-merge blocks only use ByBlockNumber. The tuple ordering ensures BLOCK_NUMBER < TIMESTAMP.

implicit_assumptions.description: All nodes in the network agree on fork activation thresholds
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Nodes with different thresholds would disagree on block validity, causing chain splits

implicit_assumptions.description: Block timestamps are reasonably accurate and cannot be arbitrarily manipulated
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Validators could manipulate timestamps to prematurely or belatedly activate forks

implicit_assumptions.description: Fork activation thresholds are set correctly by protocol developers and cannot be changed without consensus
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Incorrect thresholds could cause unintended fork activations or missed activations

implicit_assumptions.description: The transition from block-number-based to timestamp-based activation (at The Merge) is a one-time event
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If the activation mechanism changed again, the ordering logic might need revision
